gloss: to drink up; to finish drinking

definitions.gloss: to drink up; to finish drinking; to drain
definitions.explanation: To drink something completely, leaving nothing remaining. The emphasis is on finishing the entire amount of a beverage.

examples.japanese: ジュースを{飲|の}み{切|き}った。
examples.english: I drank up all the juice.

examples.japanese: {薬|くすり}は{全部|ぜんぶ}{飲|の}み{切|き}ってください。
examples.english: Please take all of the medicine.

examples.japanese: このボトルは{今日中|きょうじゅう}に{飲|の}み{切|き}らないと{炭酸|たんさん}が{抜|ぬ}けてしまう。
examples.english: If we don't finish this bottle today, it'll go flat.

examples.japanese: {牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}の{賞味期限|しょうみきげん}が{近|ちか}いから、{早|はや}めに{飲|の}み{切|き}ろう。
examples.english: The milk is near its expiration date, so let's finish it soon.

notes:
Compound of {飲|の}む (to drink) and {切|き}る (completive suffix meaning to finish completely). Part of the productive V + {切|き}る pattern where {切|き}る indicates doing something to completion.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ビールを{飲|の}み{切|き}る: to finish one's beer
- {薬|くすり}を{飲|の}み{切|き}る: to take all of the medicine
- {一気|いっき}に{飲|の}み{切|き}る: to drink up in one go
- {飲|の}み{切|き}れない: can't finish drinking (it all)

RELATED PATTERNS:
The V + {切|き}る pattern is used with many verbs to express completion:
- {食|た}べ{切|き}る: to eat up completely
- {使|つか}い{切|き}る: to use up completely
- {読|よ}み{切|き}る: to read all the way through

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {飲|の}み{干|ほ}す: to drain, drink dry — more literary; emphasizes draining a vessel completely
- {飲|の}む: to drink — basic verb without the completion nuance
